items.document_title: EMPX-H2 cryogenic probe station - technical specifications (Lake Shore Cryotronics)
items.note: Lake Shore lists station cooldown 1.25 h (LHe cycle time 3 h also includes 0.5 h vacuum pump-down and 1.25 h warmup). cooldown_time.max = 1.25 h.

items.document_title: FWPX cryogenic probe station - technical specifications (Lake Shore Cryotronics)
items.note: Lake Shore lists station cooldown 1.5 h (LHe cycle time 3.5 h also includes 0.5 h vacuum pump-down and 1.5 h warmup). cooldown_time.max = 1.5 h.

Neither the Leica EM AFS2 brochure (snapshot d9890845b97e705a) nor the Danaher product page (a8880e5eedf743c0) states a chamber cool-down time. Web search found only a Harvard facility SOP saying the chamber can take up to 1 hour to reach the starting temperature; that is a facility user note, not a manufacturer specification or a measured value in a paper, so it is not used.

The Leica EM GP2 operating manual (Version 11/17, snapshot 7efa9b6a5df40eb4, section 5.4.4 'Freezing Chamber and Cool-Down') describes cool-down by filling the Dewar with about 1.8 l LN2 but gives no cool-down time. The Leica specification page (830b972cb096a371) has no time either. Facility SOPs give a 30-60 min setup estimate for the older EM GP, a different model, so it is not used.

The Linde Kryotechnik L70/LR70 datasheet (snapshot b8cbc37283904c28) gives no cool-down or start-up time. Linde's L-Series page only says the cooling time is short, with no number. Searches found no paper reporting a measured cool-down of an L70.

The L70/LR70 datasheet (snapshot b8cbc37283904c28) gives no cool-down time with or without LN2 pre-cooling. Linde says only, qualitatively, that without pre-cooling the helium circuit starts cooling from ambient instead of 80 K. No measured value found.
The L140/LR140 datasheet (snapshot cbf4306258d04b71) gives no cool-down time. Searches found no manufacturer figure or paper reporting a measured LR140 cool-down.

The L280/LR280 datasheet (snapshot b7e7ba91743614ff) gives no cool-down time. Searches found no manufacturer figure or paper reporting a measured LR280 cool-down. An IHEP FHL-280 cool-down curve exists, but that is a different (non-Linde) plant.

The Linkam LTS420 specifications (ede560bbd69a02c5), LTS420 (68407e7751e2b5b3) and LNP96 (4dc102a14d5f1192) pages give cooling rates (LNP96 up to 100 C/min) but no time from ambient to minimum temperature. Working a time out from the rate would be an estimate, so it is not reported.

The Alpha 1-2 LSCbasic operating manual (063e830b93c931b5) mentions an ice-condenser pre-cool ('cool-down') step and a minimum condenser temperature of approx. -55 C, but gives no time to reach it. The 15 min figure in the manual is the vacuum-pump warm-up, not the condenser pull-down. The flyer (2aad6369bbd296f1), product page (30c1350736f880f9) and LSCbasic brochure (2d053232dc9a71d4) give no pull-down time either.

The Alpha 1-4/2-4 LSCbasic operating manual (cde2bb40d21f7216) describes the ice-condenser pre-cool but gives no pull-down time. Its 15 min figure is the vacuum-pump warm-up. The LSCbasic brochure (2d053232dc9a71d4) gives no time either.

The Alpha 1-4/2-4 LSCbasic operating manual (cde2bb40d21f7216) gives no time to bring the ice condenser to approx. -85 C. Its 15 min figure is the vacuum-pump warm-up. The LSCbasic brochure (2d053232dc9a71d4) gives no time either.
